ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Cars A and B start moving simultaneously from the same location on a straight, level road. The displacement-time graph of Car A and the velocity-time graph of Car B are shown in Figures A and B, respectively. Find:

1. After how much time will car B catch up with car A?
2. What is the maximum distance between the two cars before car B catches up with car A?

The displacement-time graph of Car A and the velocity-time graph of Car B are shown in Figures A and B, respectively. Find: 1. After how much time will car B catch up with car A? 2. What is the maximum distance between the two cars before car B catches up with car A?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left, Figure A is Car A's displacement-time graph, the vertical axis is labeled x/m, and the horizontal axis is labeled t/s; the straight line starts from the origin, and the dashed lines mark that when t=2 s, x=20 m. On the right, Figure B is Car B's velocity-time graph, the vertical axis is labeled v/(m·s^-1), and the horizontal axis is labeled t/s; the straight line starts from the origin, and the dashed lines mark that when t=2 s, v=4 m/s. Reasoning: From Figure A, Car A's displacement-time graph is a straight line passing through the origin, so A undergoes uniform-speed motion, with velocity v_A=20/2=10 m/s, therefore x_A(t)=10t. From Figure B, Car B's velocity-time graph is a straight line passing through the origin, so B starts from rest and undergoes uniformly accelerated motion, with acceleration a_B=4/2=2 m/s^2, therefore x_B(t)=0.5a_Bt^2=t^2. The two cars set out at the same time from the same place; when B catches up with A, their displacements are equal: 10t=t^2, and the nonzero solution is t=10 s. Before catching up, the distance between the two cars is D(t)=x_A-x_B=10t-t^2. The maximum distance satisfies dD/dt=10-2t=0, giving t=5 s, and at this time D_max=10×5-5^2=25 m.
